# Steinbach City Council Reporting

> Independent, plain-language reports on what Steinbach City Council (Steinbach, Manitoba, Canada) has said and decided, organised by topic. Each report answers one question, credits what council does well, compares Steinbach with other cities, and links every quote to its moment in the official meeting video.

- Sources: the City of Steinbach's recorded council meetings on YouTube (2015-2026) and the published minutes; other cities' own published programs for comparisons.
- Quotes are verbatim from automatic transcripts; speakers are identified by hand. Council members, the mayor and city staff are named; residents are identified by initials only.
- Each report has an 'About this page' section saying what could not be confirmed.
- Council for 2026-2030 (sworn in Nov 3, 2026): Mayor Earl Funk; Deputy Mayor Susan Penner; Councillors Damian Penner, Bill Hiebert, Jake Hiebert, Ron Falk and Greg Carlos.

## Money, growth and planning

Taxes, budgets, housing, business and the city's long-term plans.

- [Taxes, spending and priorities: how does Steinbach pay its way?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/): 152 decisions over eleven years: every budget since 2016, the five-year debt rule, reserves and growth fees, how each council member voted, council's reasons in its own words, and how Steinbach compares. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 7, 2026)
- [Steinbach in 10 to 20 years: what has council planned?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/future-planning/): 136 long-term decisions over eleven years: annexation, a second water supply, the wastewater decision, neighbours, the new community plan, how each council member acted, and how other growing cities plan. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 7, 2026)
- [Housing and development: keeping up with growth](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/housing-development/): 126 decisions over eleven years: record building, mostly apartments; every contested infill vote; the city's affordable-housing role; who pays for growth; how each council member voted, and how other councils compare. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 7, 2026)
- [Business growth and investment: what has council done?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/business-growth/): The end of the economic development office, the industrial land squeeze, the Chamber's business tax and downtown rules, compared with Winkler, Morden and Portage. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [New neighbourhoods: do drainage, sidewalks and parks arrive on time?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/new-neighbourhood-services/): Lot grading, sidewalks, playgrounds and paving in new subdivisions, wells and septic on the city's edge, and who checks, compared with Brandon, Winnipeg and Calgary. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)

## Getting around

Traffic, highways and transit.

- [Traffic in Steinbach: what can council do, and what has it done?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/): 103 decisions over eleven years: traffic counts and cost-shares on the provincial highways, stop-sign and speed requests on city streets, the traffic officer, how each council member voted, and what growing peers do. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 7, 2026)
- [A bypass around Main Street? What council says and what the traffic study shows](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/main-street-bypass/): Council says traffic comes to Steinbach rather than through it. What the city's own traffic studies show and can't show, and how Yorkton, Portage and Winkler handled their highways. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 20, 2026)
- [Can Steinbach have public transit?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/transit/): Steinbach's only transit serves seniors and people with disabilities. What council has said about anything more, and how similar-size cities run transit. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)

## Safety, health and services

Flooding, policing, health care, homelessness and the look and feel of the city.

- [Sewer backups and flooding: what has council done?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/sewer-backups/): 85 decisions over eleven years: drainage before the storms, the response to the 2024 and 2025 backups, how each council member acted, council's reasons, and what Brandon, Ottawa, Toronto and others do for homeowners. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 7, 2026)
- [Crime and policing in Steinbach](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/crime-policing/): The 18-officer RCMP contract, policing priorities, overnight security patrols and community safety officers, and how cost and crime compare with Winkler, Morden, Brandon and Portage. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Health and wellbeing: what can council do?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/health-wellbeing/): Doctor shortages, the mayor's recruitment task force, clinic space, recreation and wellbeing, and what councils in Niverville, Clarington and elsewhere do. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Homelessness in Steinbach: what's been done, and what could be](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/homelessness/): From The Bridge to the shelter zoning rules: what council has done, its reasons for not doing more, and what Brandon, Thompson and Lloydminster do. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Property standards: how does Steinbach keep rentals and yards maintained?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/property-standards/): The junk-and-weeds by-law, basement-suite safety rules and complaint-driven enforcement, compared with cities that license rentals. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Quality of life: noise, belonging, parks, recreation and arts](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/quality-of-life/): Noise enforcement, welcoming newcomers, flags and inclusion, green space, recreation and arts space, and how other councils compare. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)

## Having your say, and how council works

How to get something from council, how it hears residents, and how openly it decides.

- [Advocating to council: what has worked, and what hasn't](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/): 164 requests over eleven years: what residents and groups asked for, what they got, how each council member responded, and a playbook for advocates. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 6, 2026)
- [Public notice and having a say: do residents' objections count?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/public-notice/): How residents hear about rezonings and variances, and how often their objections changed the result, compared with Brandon, Selkirk and Lethbridge. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Behind closed doors? How much of council's work happens outside public meetings](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/behind-closed-doors/): Do unanimous votes mean decisions were made in advance? Four tests on 103 meetings, closed committee and budget sessions, and how they measure up against the Municipal Act. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Recorded public deliberation on Steinbach City Council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/council-deliberation/): How often councillors state a position and give reasons out loud, across 527 decisions. Provisional and AI-coded, with the data and method. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026 · Data: .xlsx)
- [Who moves council's public-hearing motions?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/public-hearing-motions/): How many of the 203 motions after public hearings each council member moved and seconded, each listed with a plain summary and its moment in the video. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 19, 2026)

## Follow-up: what's still open

What the 2022–2026 term left unfinished, and practical steps for the council that follows.

- [Unfinished business: questions for Steinbach's outgoing councillors](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/action-list/): Promises, referrals and decisions from the 2022–2026 term that the public record leaves open, each with dated quotes and a question that can be answered with a date, a number or a document. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Serving Steinbach well: an action plan for council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/action-list/candidate-action-plan/): Practical steps drawn from these reports, written for candidates and now for the new council: open, reasoned decision-making first, then process and policy gaps by topic. (Based on meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026)

## 2026 election (archive)

What the candidates said before the October 28, 2026 election, with full transcripts.

- [2026 council candidates' forum: every question, every answer](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/candidate-forum-2026/): All 10 candidates' answers at the Chamber of Commerce forum, side by side and linked to the video, with the incumbents' answers checked against their council record. (Chamber of Commerce forum, Oct 15, 2026 · Updated Oct 16, 2026)
  - [the full forum transcript](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/candidate-forum-2026-transcript/)
- [Residents' election forum: what residents asked, and how four candidates answered](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/residents-forum-2026/): Residents' questions on housing, health, transportation and quality of life, with full answers from the four candidates who attended. (Residents' forum, Oct 7, 2026 · Updated Oct 16, 2026)
  - [the full forum transcript](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/residents-forum-2026-transcript/)
- [Candidates in writing: growth and housing, flooding, and public safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/candidate-interviews-2026/): All 10 candidates' written answers to SteinbachOnline on three issues, side by side, with record checks for the incumbents. (SteinbachOnline, Oct 7–15, 2026 · Updated Oct 16, 2026)

- [2022–2026: Mayor Earl Funk’s second council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/housing-development/terms/2022-2026/): Steinbach City Council's housing and development record in the 2022–2026 term: record permits, development fees kept to 5% a year, split votes on infill and parking, a new community plan, and the wastewater bill.

- [2014–2018: Mayor Chris Goertzen’s council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/sewer-backups/terms/2014-2018/): Steinbach City Council on drainage, sewers and flooding from December 2015 to November 2018: the Home Street North swale, rules for new development, pipe renewal, and where members split.
- [2018–2022: Mayor Earl Funk’s first council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/sewer-backups/terms/2018-2022/): Steinbach City Council on drainage, sewers and flooding from November 2018 to October 2022: ponds and relined pipes, runoff rules for development, a 2019 storm and a 2022 disaster-aid request, and where members split.
- [2022–2026: Mayor Earl Funk’s second council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/sewer-backups/terms/2022-2026/): Steinbach City Council on sewer backups, flooding and drainage from November 2022 to October 2026: growth-framed sewer work, the 2024 and 2025 storms, two disaster-aid refusals, the flood plan, a new drainage by-law and a lawsuit.
- [The story by term](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/sewer-backups/terms/): Steinbach City Council's record on sewer backups, flooding and drainage told council by council and year by year, 2015 to 2026, with what the new 2026–2030 council inherits.
- [How Steinbach compares](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/compare/): How Steinbach's tax rate, debt, reserves, growth fees and budget openness compare with Brandon, Winkler, Morden, Portage la Prairie, Selkirk, Niverville and others in 2026.
- [Bill Hiebert: taxes, budgets and spending](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/members/bill-hiebert/): What Bill Hiebert said and did on Steinbach's taxes, budgets, debt and spending, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.

- [Council’s reasons, in its own words](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/reasons/): The eight reasons Steinbach City Council has given for how it taxes, borrows and spends, 2015 to 2026, in members' own words, with the counterpoints.
- [Every decision and debate on taxes and spending](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/record/): Every Steinbach City Council decision and debate on taxes, budgets, debt, fees and spending from December 2015 to November 2026, filterable, with spreadsheet downloads.
- [2014–2018: Mayor Chris Goertzen’s council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/terms/2014-2018/): Steinbach City Council's taxes, budgets and spending in the 2014–2018 term: tax freezes, the RCMP cost jump, the arts centre and the golf club land deal.
- [2018–2022: Mayor Earl Funk’s first council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/terms/2018-2022/): Steinbach City Council's taxes, budgets and spending in the 2018–2022 term: frozen rates, COVID-19, who pays for local improvements, and saving for the event centre.
- [2022–2026: Mayor Earl Funk’s second council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/terms/2022-2026/): Steinbach City Council's taxes, budgets and spending in the 2022–2026 term: the event centre, a 5.1% increase, holding the rate in a reassessment year, and the wastewater bill ahead.
- [The story by term](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/terms/): Steinbach's taxes and spending told council by council and year by year, 2015 to 2026, with what the new 2026–2030 council inherits.
- [How Steinbach compares](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/compare/): How Steinbach's traffic planning, highway partnerships, speed limits, traffic calming and enforcement compare with Brandon, Winkler, Morden, Portage la Prairie, Selkirk, Niverville, Cochrane and Okotoks.
- [Bill Hiebert: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/bill-hiebert/): What Bill Hiebert said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Cari Penner: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/cari-penner/): What Cari Penner said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.

- [Damian Penner: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/damian-penner/): What Damian Penner said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Earl Funk: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/earl-funk/): What Earl Funk said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Council members on traffic and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/): How each Steinbach council member voted and spoke on traffic, congestion and road safety from 2015 to 2026, with every split vote.
- [Jac Siemens: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/jac-siemens/): What Jac Siemens said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Jake Hiebert: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/jake-hiebert/): What Jake Hiebert said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [John Fehr: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/john-fehr/): What John Fehr said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Michael Zwaagstra: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/michael-zwaagstra/): What Michael Zwaagstra said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Susan Penner: traffic, congestion and road safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/members/susan-penner/): What Susan Penner said and did on traffic, congestion and road safety in Steinbach, 2015 to 2026, with split votes and quotes.
- [Council’s reasons, in its own words](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/reasons/): The eight reasons Steinbach City Council has given for not doing more about traffic and road safety, 2015 to 2026, in members' own words, with residents' counterpoints and the facts.
- [Every decision and debate on traffic and congestion](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/record/): Every Steinbach City Council decision and debate on traffic and congestion (Main Street and the highways, city streets, stop signs and signals, speed and enforcement) from December 2015 to November 2026, filterable, with spreadsheet downloads.
- [2014–2018: Mayor Chris Goertzen’s council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/terms/2014-2018/): Steinbach City Council and traffic in the 2014–2018 term: the last of a shared PTH 12 program, four years of counts before Industrial Road got signals, and Loewen Boulevard named the worst corner.
- [2018–2022: Mayor Earl Funk’s first council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/terms/2018-2022/): Steinbach City Council and traffic in the 2018–2022 term: city speed limits, a traffic officer for street racing, the Loewen Boulevard rebuild financed, the Giesbrecht signals requested, and infill approved without traffic studies.
- [2022–2026: Mayor Earl Funk’s second council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/terms/2022-2026/): Steinbach City Council and traffic in the 2022–2026 term: PTH 12 signal timing fixed, a stop sign defeated 3–4, the Loewen Boulevard rebuild, a school zone beyond staff advice, the automobile city, and the Giesbrecht lights at last.
- [The story by term](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/terms/): Steinbach City Council's record on traffic and road safety told council by council and year by year, 2015 to 2026, with what the new 2026–2030 council inherits.
